cat > /app/eval.scm << 'SCMEOF'
;; eval.scm - a metacircular evaluator for the Scheme-like language
;; implemented by interp.py.
;;
;; Reads exactly one line from STDIN: the path of a .scm file to interpret.
;; All remaining input is captured and supplied to the interpreted program
;; (through its getchr / read).  Output of the program goes to STDOUT.
;;
;; This file can interpret any program the host interpreter can run,
;; including itself.

(define $stdin #f)

;; ---------- small utilities ----------

(define (cadr x) (car (cdr x)))
(define (caddr x) (car (car (cdr x))))
(define (cddr x) (cdr (cdr x)))
(define (cdddr x) (cdr (cdr (cdr x))))

(define (m-length ls)
  (if (null? ls) 0 (+ 1 (m-length (cdr ls)))))

(define (nth n ls)
  (if (= n 0) (car ls) (nth (- n 1) (cdr ls))))

(define (list-reverse ls)
  (let ((loop (lambda (acc xs)
                (if (null? xs)
                    acc
                    (loop (cons (car xs) acc) (cdr xs))))))
    (loop '() ls)))

;; is-not-false v is true unless v is exactly #f (the host treats every
;; value as truthy except #f in `if`, and in `cond` tests likewise).
(define (is-not-false v)
  (not (not v)))

;; ---------- error handling ----------
;; The host interpreter prints "Error: <msg>" and halts when a SchemeError
;; is raised.  We print the message and then raise a Python exception so
;; that execution stops the same way.

(define (m-error msg)
  (display msg)
  (newline)
  (chr -1))

;; Mimics the host crashing on unexpected end of input (its getchr dies in
;; ord('') and its read dies with EOFError when a line has no characters).
(define (m-crash)
  (chr -1))

;; ---------- metacircular environments ----------
;; An environment is a two-element list (entries parent): entries is a
;; list of two-element (name value) pairs, parent is another environment
;; or #f.

(define (make-env entries parent)
  (cons entries (cons parent '())))

(define (make-entry name value)
  (cons name (cons value '())))

(define (add-entry entries name value)
  (cons (make-entry name value) entries))

(define (m-define! env name value)
  (set-car! env (add-entry (car env) name value)))

(define (alist-ref name entries)
  (if (null? entries)
      '$unbound$
      (if (eq? (caar entries) name)
          (cadar entries)
          (alist-ref name (cdr entries)))))

(define (env-ref name env)
  (if (eq? env #f)
      '$unbound$
      (let ((r (alist-ref name (car env))))
        (if (eq? r '$unbound$)
            (env-ref name (cadr env))
            r))))

(define (m-lookup name env)
  (let ((v (env-ref name env)))
    (if (eq? v '$unbound$)
        (m-error "Error: Undefined variable")
        v)))

(define (alist-set name value entries)
  (if (null? entries)
      '()
      (if (eq? (caar entries) name)
          (set-car! (cdr (car entries)) value)
          (alist-set name value (cdr entries)))))

(define (m-set! env name value)
  (if (eq? env #f)
      (m-error "Error: Undefined variable")
      (if (eq? (alist-ref name (car env)) '$unbound$)
          (m-set! (cadr env) name value)
          (begin
            (alist-set name value (car env))
            '()))))

;; ---------- closures ----------
;; Closures of the interpreted program are tagged lists:
;;   ($mproc$ params body env)

(define (make-closure params body env)
  (cons '$mproc$ (cons params (cons body (cons env '())))))

(define (is-closure? v)
  (and (pair? v) (eq? (car v) '$mproc$)))

;; A "primitive" is anything that is not a datum: not a number, not a
;; symbol, not a string, not a list.  These are the host's built-in
;; functions (or closures coming from an outer evaluation level).
(define (m-prim? v)
  (and (not (number? v))
       (not (string? v))
       (not (symbol? v))
       (not (null? v))
       (not (pair? v))))

;; ---------- application ----------

(define (m-bind params args)
  (if (null? params)
      '()
      (cons (make-entry (car params) (car args))
            (m-bind (cdr params) (cdr args)))))

src = open('eval.scm').read()
stack = []
i = 0
line = 1
errors = []
while i < len(src):
    ch = src[i]
    if ch == '\n':
        line += 1; i += 1; continue
    if ch == ';':
        while i < len(src) and src[i] != '\n': i += 1
        continue
    if ch == '"':
        i += 1
        while i < len(src) and src[i] != '"':
            if src[i] == '\\': i += 1
            if src[i] == '\n': line += 1
            i += 1
        i += 1
        continue
    if ch == '(':
        stack.append(line); i += 1; continue
    if ch == ')':
        if not stack:
            errors.append(('extra )', line))
        else:
            stack.pop()
        i += 1; continue
    i += 1
for l in stack:
    errors.append(('unclosed ( at line', l))
print('errors:', errors if errors else 'NONE')

        continue

            i += 1
        i += 1

        continue
    if ch == '(':
        if depth == 0: start = line; buf = []
        depth += 1; buf.append('('); i += 1; continue
    if ch == ')':
        depth -= 1; buf.append(')')
        if depth == 0:
            forms.append((start, ''.join(buf)))
        i += 1; continue
    # collect raw text for display

        buf.append(ch)
    i += 1
print('total forms:', len(forms), 'final depth:', depth)
for s, b in forms:
    o, c = b.count('('), b.count(')')
    if o != c:
        print(f'line {s}: opens={o} closes={c} delta={o-c} :: {b[:60]}...')
